主要内容: Treasury Secretary Janet L. Yellen addressed inquiries from State Attorneys General about the implementation of Section 9901 of the American Rescue Plan Act. The provision provides funds to States, territories, Tribal governments, and localities to manage the economic consequences of the pandemic. Congress has given States considerable flexibility to use the funds but has also placed limitations to ensure the money is used for its intended purposes. Specifically, the Act prohibits using the funds to offset a reduction in net tax revenue from certain state law changes. Yellen emphasized that the Act does not prevent States from enacting a broad variety of tax cuts, as long as the funds are not used to offset those cuts. Treasury is developing further guidance to clarify the implementation of the provision and will provide it before states must submit a certification under § 602(d)(1). The letter was sent on March 23, 2021, and was circulated to multiple state officials, including those from Arizona, West Virginia, Massachusetts, and others. The response aimed to clarify the guidelines for the use of ARP funds and to foster cooperation between federal and state authorities.
